definition: Mandatory registration of your home address at the local Bürgeramt (Citizens' Office). Required by German law within 2 weeks of moving in.
The elected student government that represents all students, organizes events, manages the semester ticket, and provides legal advice.
German government financial support for students who meet income and enrollment requirements. Apply at the Studentenwerk.
The official process of registering as a student at the university. You receive an Immatrikulationsbescheinigung (enrollment certificate) as proof.
A written examination, usually held at the end of the semester. You must register in QIS before the deadline to be allowed to sit it.
Official proof that you passed a course or fulfilled a requirement. Some courses require a Schein to qualify for the final exam.
The fee you pay each semester to re-enroll. It usually covers your student card, semester ticket (public transport), and a contribution to the student union.
A regional public transport pass included in your Semesterbeitrag. Allows unlimited travel on buses and trains within the defined area during the semester.
The contact hours for a course per week. A 2 SWS course meets for 2 hours every week during the semester (roughly 15 weeks).
The university's online learning platform. Used for course enrollment, downloading materials, receiving announcements, and submitting assignments.
Online portal for registering for exams, viewing grades, and checking your academic progress. Critical to use every semester.
The standard credit system used across European universities. One ECTS typically represents about 25–30 hours of student workload.
The office that manages exam administration, grade records, and degree certification.
The administrative office that handles enrollment, de-registration, enrollment certificates, and address changes.

translation: Environmental Planning and Environmental Technology (degree program)
definition: One of UCB's core degree programs focusing on environmental sciences and technology.
A degree program at UCB combining business management with sustainability and legal aspects.
A traditional university lecture where the professor presents material to a large group. Usually mandatory attendance is not tracked.
A smaller, practice-oriented session that accompanies a lecture. Often attendance is mandatory.
Designated times when professors or staff are available for personal consultations. Check Stud.IP or the professor's door for their schedule.
The formal process of leaving the university. Required when you finish your degree or transfer. You must return your student card and library books.
A form your landlord fills out confirming you live at a specific address. Required for the Anmeldung (address registration).
The public or private health insurance provider. All students must be insured. Popular public options: TK (Techniker Krankenkasse), AOK, DAK.
